blocking.section: Threat model and trust boundaries (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14 answer); Transport security (8091 row)
blocking.issue: The document picks option (a) of OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14. That option means "amend pack 8.4 (8091) and System overview", but the document never states or proposes the amendment. It also maps the new crossings incompletely. Control plane and GitOps lists token `Enroll` on 8091 (TB-5), token replica join (TB-11), HMAC webhooks, Ruralz Control as an OCI registry client, a Kubernetes client (service account) and the relay on 8092 (TB-13). This document maps them only to TB-5, TB-7, TB-8 and TB-13, and drops TB-11 and the Kubernetes client. The transport row for 8091 says "mTLS, TLS 1.3 only", which is pack 8.4's current rule. Control plane and GitOps, however, makes 8091 request a client certificate without requiring one, because `Enroll` authenticates with a token. The owner of the question has therefore adopted an amendment that its own transport table contradicts, and nothing records a pending pack change.
blocking.evidence: Line 109: "For OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14, option (a), its new crossings map to TB-5, TB-7, TB-8 and TB-13." Line 123: "| 8091 (TB-5), 8092 (TB-11), relay (TB-13) | mTLS, TLS 1.3 only | Disjoint CAs, so a Node key cannot join Raft |". Pack 8.4, 8091 row: "mTLS, per-Node enrollment certificate". Control plane and GitOps line 321: "The 8091 listener requests but does not require a client certificate: `Enroll` needs a valid token". Line 589: "token `Enroll` (TB-5), token replica join (TB-11), HMAC webhooks, Ruralz Control as OCI registry client ... and Kubernetes client (service account), and the relay on 8092 (TB-13)". Line 607: "OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14 | Should pack 8.4 (8091) and System overview add token `Enroll` (TB-5) ... | (a) Amend (proposed)".
blocking.fix: (1) Rewrite line 109 as: "For OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-14, option (a): token `Enroll` maps to TB-5, token replica join to TB-11, webhooks and the Kubernetes client to TB-7, Ruralz Control's registry client to TB-8, and the relay to TB-13; the pack 8.4 8091 row and System overview TB-5 need amending (OQ-security-and-identity-29)." Alternatively, add a new Open question owned by system-overview that proposes the exact pack 8.4 wording, for example "mTLS with a per-Node enrollment certificate; `Enroll` only: server-authenticated TLS plus a one-time token". (2) Split the 8091 transport row: "8091 (TB-5) | TLS 1.3; client certificate required for every RPC except `Enroll`, which needs a one-time token (proposed, pack 8.4 amendment)". (3) Add a `ctl -->|"TB-8"| oci` edge to Figure 1.

blocking.issue: The engine-memory bound contradicts System overview's Compile before swap in two ways. (1) System overview keeps K = 2 retired snapshots and gives peak configuration memory as (K + 2) times the snapshot size (hypothesis), which is four copies while a candidate compiles. This document claims engine memory stays under three times the ceiling (target). (2) The "Node compile budget" in System overview is a time budget ("2 s or less on one core (target)"), and the Configuration model uses the term the same way. It is not a memory budget, so 64 MiB of engine data cannot "count against" it. The line also changes the tag from System overview's (hypothesis) to (target) without any benchmark.
blocking.evidence: Line 291: "A Revision-wide ceiling of 64 MiB of engine data and 50,000 entities (target), checked by `ruralz bundle validate` (code: OQ-security-and-identity-30), counts against the Node compile budget ([System overview](01-system-overview.md#compile-before-swap)), so with two retired snapshots engine memory stays under three times it (target)." System overview lines 340 to 342: "At most K = 2 retired snapshots are kept (target)" and "Building router structures and chains for 10,000 Routes takes 2 s or less on one core (target) ... Peak configuration memory is (K + 2) times snapshot size (hypothesis)". Configuration model line 823: "The Node compile budget is separate ([System overview](01-system-overview.md))" (a validation-time context).
blocking.fix: Replace the clause with: "counts toward snapshot size, so peak engine memory is at most (K + 2) = 4 times the ceiling, 256 MiB (hypothesis), per [System overview](01-system-overview.md#compile-before-swap); content-digest reuse lowers it when engines do not change. Engine compilation also counts against the Node compile time budget." If a lower bound is intended, say how the candidate's copy is avoided, and tag the figure (hypothesis).

blocking.section: Control plane security (Signed Revisions and Plugin artifacts)
blocking.issue: The document states the OCI anti-rollback rule as a present-tense MUST, although its own Open question marks the rule as a proposed pack 8.14 amendment. This is the same pattern the previous round fixed for Secrets rules 5 to 7. The rule also changes file-mode behavior that the foundation documents fix. Pack 8.1 and 8.3, and System overview's Deployment modes, describe file-mode change delivery as "CI replaces the directory or publishes a digest", and CI rolls back by publishing an older digest. If Nodes reject older sequences, that rollback is refused. To reject older sequences after a restart, a Node must also persist a sequence high-water mark, and pack 8.11 lists no such state. OQ-security-and-identity-26 names only pack 8.14.
blocking.evidence: Line 472: "`ruralz bundle push` MUST add signed Environment and sequence annotations, and file-mode Nodes reject other Environments and older sequences (OQ-security-and-identity-26)." Line 552: "| OQ-security-and-identity-26 | Which signed annotations bind an OCI Revision? | (a) Environment and sequence, amending pack section 8.14 (proposed); (b) Digest |". Pack 8.11: "A Node persists only the following under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`" (identity, Last-Known-Good and candidate, disposable caches). System overview Deployment modes: "CI replaces the directory or publishes a digest; not a Rollout".
blocking.fix: Reword line 472 as: "Proposed, pending OQ-security-and-identity-26: `ruralz bundle push` adds signed Environment and sequence annotations, and file-mode Nodes reject other Environments and older sequences; a rollback re-pushes the older Revision with a new sequence. Until then, Nodes check only digest and signature." Say where the high-water sequence persists, for example beside the candidate under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/lkg/`. Add pack 8.11, and the System overview file-mode rollback wording, to the amendments that OQ-security-and-identity-26 lists.
